paths.description: Public entry page and initial recon. Failed because the edge returned a Forbidden bot-denial document.

findings.summary: Automated crawlers are denied access to the public entry page.
findings.evidence: The discoverability primitive fetched the raw document with crawler user agent and received HTTP 403. Browser and crawler screenshots both show only a Forbidden support page; /robots.txt also returned 403.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the bot/WAF policy so legitimate search and accessibility tooling can fetch public content, and serve a crawlable robots.txt. Keep abusive traffic controls targeted rather than denying all non-human clients.

findings.summary: The public URL and indexing support files return unsuccessful HTTP status codes.
findings.evidence: The HAR records two 403 responses for the navigation, while independent fetches of /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml also returned 403. A successful 2xx document could not be reached.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a successful 2xx response containing the canonical public page to legitimate crawlers and expose robots.txt and sitemap.xml consistently through the edge security layer.

taskList.title: Permit legitimate crawlers and audit clients through the WAF, then expose successful public indexing responses
